name: New Orleans
tagline: Where the Music Never Stops Playing
description: The birthplace of jazz and the undisputed culinary capital of the American South, built on 300 years of French, Spanish, African, and Creole culture layered into every block. A city where brass bands lead funeral processions, strangers dance together on Frenchmen Street at midnight, and a Tuesday lunch at a century-old restaurant is treated as sacred.

identity.vibe: A 300-year-old party town with a Ph.D. in culture — equal parts hedonistic and deeply soulful, where every meal is an event and every night has a soundtrack.

nexus_grid.title: Food & Drink
nexus_grid.description: The single biggest reason people come to New Orleans — from century-old Creole institutions to James Beard-winning newcomers.

nexus_grid.title: Live Music & Nightlife
nexus_grid.description: The birthplace of jazz — Frenchmen Street, Preservation Hall, and 100+ venues where world-class music plays every single night, most of it free.

nexus_grid.title: Festivals & Events
nexus_grid.description: More festivals per capita than any American city — Mardi Gras, Jazz Fest, French Quarter Fest, ESSENCE, Voodoo, and a packed year-round calendar.

nexus_grid.title: Live Music & Nightlife
nexus_grid.description: Jazz clubs, Frenchmen Street, Bourbon Street

modes.label: Foodie
modes.description: Creole, Cajun, Michelin-starred, and everything between — eat your way through the culinary capital of America.

modes.label: Nightlife
modes.description: Frenchmen Street jazz, Bourbon Street chaos, cocktail palaces, and dive bars — all in a city that never closes.

modes.label: Culture & History
modes.description: 300 years of French, Spanish, African, and Creole heritage — museums, architecture, jazz, cemeteries, and living traditions.

modes.label: Romantic
modes.description: Candlelit courtyards, tasting menus, converted-church cocktail bars, and streetcar rides through the Garden District.

modes.label: Family
modes.description: The WWII Museum, Audubon Zoo, streetcar rides, beignets, and swamp tours — family-friendly New Orleans is incredible.

modes.label: Chill
modes.description: City Park oaks, Bywater bike rides, wine gardens, po'boys by the river, and slow afternoons on a porch.

modes.label: Adventure
modes.description: Swamp tours, kayaking, bike trails, and getting lost in neighborhoods most tourists never see.

modes.label: Festival Mode
modes.description: Mardi Gras, Jazz Fest, French Quarter Fest, ESSENCE, Voodoo — the city with more festivals per capita than anywhere in America.

transit.local_transport: Highly walkable within the French Quarter, Marigny, and CBD. RTA streetcars ($1.25/ride, $3 Jazzy Pass daily) run the St. Charles line (Garden District/Uptown), Canal Street, and Riverfront. Uber/Lyft widely available. Blue Bikes bike-share ($8/24hrs). You do NOT need a car — parking in the Quarter is $40-65/night and streets are narrow. Streetcar + walking + rideshare covers everything.

_legacy_transit.label: Drive
_legacy_transit.text: Baton Rouge: 80 mi via I-10 East (1 hr 15 min). Houston: 350 mi via I-10 West (5 hrs). Gulf Coast/Biloxi: 90 mi via I-10 East (1 hr 20 min).

_legacy_transit.label: Train
_legacy_transit.text: Amtrak serves Union Passenger Terminal downtown: City of New Orleans (Chicago), Crescent (New York/Atlanta), Sunset Limited (LA/Houston), and the new Mardi Gras Service (Mobile, AL via Gulf Coast). Station is walking distance to Superdome and streetcar.

_legacy_transit.label: Fly
_legacy_transit.text: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY) — 15 miles west of downtown, 25-40 min by car/rideshare. Direct flights from most major US cities. Airport shuttle $24/person, taxi flat rate $36 to French Quarter, rideshare $20-35.

side_trips.name: Plantation Country (River Road)
side_trips.pitch: Drive River Road between New Orleans and Baton Rouge for a string of antebellum plantation houses. Whitney Plantation focuses specifically on enslaved people's stories — the only one that does.

side_trips.name: Biloxi / Mississippi Gulf Coast
side_trips.distance: 90 min drive or Amtrak Mardi Gras Service
side_trips.pitch: Casino-beach town with a completely different vibe. Take the new Amtrak route for a car-free day trip. Casinos, white sand beaches, and Gulf seafood.

side_trips.name: Cajun Country (Lafayette)
side_trips.pitch: The heart of Cajun culture — zydeco dance halls, boudin trail, crawfish farms, and a completely different Louisiana than New Orleans.

side_trips.name: Bay St. Louis, Mississippi
side_trips.pitch: Charming Gulf Coast art town with galleries, great food, and a laid-back vibe. Easy Amtrak day trip on the new Mardi Gras Service.

concierge.name: The Second Line
concierge.greeting: Ayyyy, welcome to the Crescent City, baby! I'm your personal guide to everything New Orleans — the food that'll change your life, the music that'll keep you up past your bedtime, and the spots the locals don't want you to know about. But I'm feelin' generous. What you lookin' for?

_legacy.hero_title: New Orleans — Hot Nights, Hotter Music
_legacy.hero_sub: ESSENCE Fest takes over the Superdome, Satchmo SummerFest fills the Quarter, and every restaurant cranks the A/C while you feast on crawfish and frozen daiquiris.
